submitter: architecture-review workstream (D11 layer 1b guard, owner ruling D12=1b)
rationale:
OWNER RULING 2026-07-29: D12 = option 1b. This is that guard, and it is
submitted SEPARATELY from the markdown corpus it exists to guard.

WHY ITS OWN SUBMISSION. This alters a SHARED mechanism -- how every diagnosis run
labels its evidence. The 2026-07-28 owner ruling is explicit that a shared-mechanism
change is architecture-scope even when additive and small, and that the answer to
one is to "route the seam to architecture review on its own merits" rather than let
it ride inside a feature plan. Folding it into the markdown plan (corr 7ba5b8c4,
round 9) would also repeat that sequence's own failure mode: rounds 4-6 died because
each objection was answered by adding mechanism INSIDE the plan, and each addition
became fresh surface. So the markdown plan is HELD at round 8 until this is decided.

WHAT IS BROKEN. The diagnosis loop gates a CONFIRMED verdict on carrying BOTH
evidence families -- a static citation showing the mechanism in code, and a
state/runtime citation showing it occurring (pkg/diagnose/step.go tierCovered).
The static family IS this index: pkg/diagnose/loop.go:60 defines
`TierStatic Tier = iota // code_symbols + \d (T1)`. Today that is sound because the
index holds Go only. The moment markdown enters it, a section of bugs_open/*.md can
satisfy the "mechanism in code" half -- and the assembler will have told the
verdicter, in words, that it is code.

THE FAILURE IS A HEADING, WHICH IS WHY THE FIX IS ONE. diagnose_assemble_bundle_action.go
:267-271 emits, unconditionally, over everything the index returns:
  "## Code search results (from the code_symbols index -- STATIC tier)"
  "These answer code questions a previous iteration asked. They are CODE, so
   they are static evidence..."
The comment above it states the design intent exactly: "the surest way to keep that
true is to never let them appear under a heading a verdicter could read as observed
state. The heading says so in words, BECAUSE THE MODEL READS THE HEADING AND NOT
THIS COMMENT." The guard is a rendered string aimed at an LLM. A wrong string is the
whole defect, and a corrected string is the whole fix.

THE PLATFORM ALREADY SOLVED THIS ONE LEVEL DOWN, and I am reusing its vocabulary
rather than inventing one. diagnose_code_lookup_action.go:507-511 carries the
[body]/[decl] marker precisely because "a reviewer who cannot tell them apart will
read a doc-comment mention as an implementation." This adds [doc] to that same
discriminator, in the same function, for the same reason at one level up.

ONE EDIT COVERS BOTH LANES, and that is measured, not hoped. Two lanes answer code
checks -- the council/verify tier (diagnose_code_lookup) and diagnose_load_runtime --
and diagnose_load_runtime_action.go:436-438 says of the helper it calls: "answered
from the code_symbols index by the SAME helpers the council's verify tier uses
(diagnose_code_lookup_action.go -- same package, so this is reuse, not a second
implementation)." It calls answerCodeCheck at :479. So tagging inside answerCodeCheck
reaches both renderers; there is no sibling copy to drift.

BLAST RADIUS, MEASURED BEFORE SUBMITTING, NOT LEFT FOR THE REVIEWER. Live today:
code_symbols holds 5,017 rows across five Go kinds (func 3068, method 1026, struct
861, interface 33, alias 29) and ZERO doc rows, and code_symbols_kind_check still
refuses 'doc'. So kind='doc' is UNREPRESENTABLE at the moment this ships: every
tagging branch is dead code on arrival and the only observable change is the bundle
heading's wording. THIS IS DELIBERATE AND IT IS THE POINT -- the guard lands before
the hazard can exist, which is the ordering the 07-28 ruling asks for and which
shipping them together would not give.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO. It does not add a tier, change tierCovered, or touch
pkg/diagnose at all -- the tier contract in Go is untouched. It changes what the
verdicter is TOLD about rows it is already being shown. A third path exists
(lookup_code_symbols' code_results -> scopeFromCodeResults, assemble_bundle:596)
but it derives path:Symbol SCOPE entries and renders no evidence text, so it is a
scope-pollution question for the markdown plan, not a citation question for this
one. Named here so its absence from the edits is a decision, not an oversight.

plan.summary: D12 option 1b, owner-ruled 2026-07-29: mark doc-kind rows [doc] in the shared code-answer renderer and stop the evidence bundle telling the verdicter that everything from the code_symbols index is CODE. Submitted on its OWN correlation, ahead of the markdown corpus it guards, because it alters a shared mechanism (every diagnosis run) and is inert until that corpus exists.

edits.rationale: The single shared renderer for BOTH code-answer lanes (diagnose_load_runtime_action.go:436-438 names it as reuse, and calls it at :479), so one edit closes both. All three check kinds gain `kind` in their SELECT -- which is the point, not a side effect: guardian's round-8 objection was that NOTHING distinguishes a doc row at read time, and selecting the column is what makes the distinction exist where the reader is. Doc rows are buffered into their own block emitted AFTER the code rows under a heading naming what they are, rather than interleaved -- a marker on a line the verdicter skims is weaker than a section it must cross. NOT REUSING nothing: this EXTENDS the existing [body]/[decl] discriminator at :507-511 rather than adding a parallel one.

THE LOAD-BEARING EDIT, and the seam. The heading is the guard -- the comment above it says so: 'the heading says so in words, because the model reads the heading and not this comment.' Today it asserts 'They are CODE' over everything the index returns, which becomes FALSE the day markdown is indexed and is the specific sentence that would launder a doc excerpt into a static citation. The replacement keeps the static-tier claim for code, states the [doc] exception in the same breath, and preserves the existing sentence that a confirm still needs a state/runtime citation -- that clause is doing separate work (it stops code-only confirms) and must not be lost in the rewording. The line at :239 ('the static tier cannot reach it (code_symbols indexes .go only)') is left alone deliberately: it is a true statement about TODAY and becomes the markdown plan's to correct, in the commit that makes it false.

edits.rationale: This change is INERT on arrival (kind='doc' is unrepresentable until the markdown plan ships), so every DB-shaped assertion would pass identically against a pod that never received it. The verification therefore has to be the BINARY, and it has an unusually good marker: the change DELETES a string. Per the standing discipline the best marker is a string the change removed, plus a positive control -- this has both, measured on the live pod before the change.
edits.sketch:
# VERIFY — D12 option 1b guard

## 1. The binary, and nothing else can stand in for it

    POD=$(kubectl -n ai-persona-system get pods -l app=agent-chassis \
          -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
    for s in 'They are CODE' 'docTag' 'answerCodeCheck'; do
      kubectl -n ai-persona-system exec $POD -- sh -c \
        "strings /app/agent-chassis | grep -c '$s'"; done

    MEASURED PRE-CHANGE (2026-07-29, live pod):
      'They are CODE'   1   -> MUST BECOME 0   (the string this change DELETES)
      'docTag'          0   -> MUST BECOME >0  (the symbol it ADDS)
      'answerCodeCheck' 8   -> stays >0        (positive control)

    A deleted string going to 0 cannot be faked by a stale cached layer the way
    an added string can be missed by a bad grep. Re-run after ANY roll you did
    not perform yourself.

## 2. Behaviour is unchanged for code rows — the negative control

    SELECT kind, count(*) FROM code_symbols GROUP BY kind;   -- 0 rows of 'doc'

    With no doc rows, every tagging branch is dead: a code answer must render
    byte-identically to before. Run any `symbol` code_check through a diagnosis
    and diff the rendered answer against a pre-change run — expect NO diff.

## 3. The guard is only exercised when the markdown plan ships

    Deliberate. This file's assertions do NOT prove the guard WORKS, only that it
    is PRESENT and harmless. The working proof belongs to corr 7ba5b8c4's VERIFY,
    which must assert that a kind='doc' hit renders under the prose heading and
    carries [doc]. Stated here so nobody reads section 1 as coverage it is not.

plan.risks: (1) THE ONE THING THAT COULD REGRESS TODAY is the code path, because the doc path cannot execute: with 0 doc rows every tagging branch is dead and a code answer must render byte-identically. The VERIFY's negative control is a no-diff check on a real code_check, not an assertion that the new branch works. (2) BLAST RADIUS IS EVERY DIAGNOSIS RUN, and it is the heading text -- stated plainly rather than minimised. That is exactly why this is submitted on its own correlation instead of inside the markdown plan. (3) THE REWORDING MUST NOT DROP THE EXISTING CLAUSE. 'A confirm still needs a state/runtime citation showing it happening' is doing separate work (it stops code-only confirms) and is preserved verbatim; losing it while fixing a different sentence in the same block is the realistic way to make this change harmful. (4) A LONGER HEADING COSTS PROMPT BUDGET in every bundle. ~5 lines against bundles whose max_body_chars default is 60000. Named because it is a real cost, not a nil one. (5) NOT COVERED, DELIBERATELY: lookup_code_symbols' code_results -> scopeFromCodeResults (assemble_bundle:596) turns rows into path:Symbol SCOPE entries and renders no evidence text, so it is a scope-pollution question owned by the markdown plan, not a citation question here. Its absence from the edits is a decision. (6) DEPLOY: Go, so inert until the image rolls -- and unusually, an un-rolled deploy is HARMLESS here rather than a degrade, because the thing it guards cannot exist yet. Verified by the deleted string going to 0, never by git or the tag.
